name: Acid Marsh
pitch: A drowned agri-dome turned into a green, steaming swamp where the sky itself burns: run between roofs when the rain comes, and push the creep back with fire.

theme.floor: Black mud #1d221a with moss patches #3f5a2a; boardwalk planks #6b5a3e; acid pools toxic green #7cff3a; shallow water #2a5d7a turned olive #3d5a3a
theme.walls: Rusted dome struts and greenhouse frames as B blocks, weathered steel #5a5f52 with green corrosion streaks #8fbf4a; crates as rotten feed bins
theme.lighting: Key light sickly yellow-green #d6e88a, intensity 0.8, 60 deg overhead through broken dome glass; ambient #39452e at 0.5; acid pools carry green point lights #7cff3a (3 m) every 3rd cell; rain pulses lerp the key to #9cff6a
theme.fog: Dense swamp haze #6e7f4a, exponential 0.035, thicker near the floor
theme.signature_detail: Every cover roof drips green after rain and its slab hisses with steam; the HUD shows a 'RAIN IN 3' siren pip and the sky tints green before every pulse
theme.audio: Insects and dripping bed, the dome siren before rain, acid sizzle on metal, Spitter gurgles carrying through the haze

signature: The rain sets the rhythm. Every 20 s you have 3 s to reach a roof, and 4 s of rain where open ground costs 6 HP per half second; but the rain also eats 4% of every exposed enemy's HP per tick, so the best players stand under a roof and let the swarm melt in the open around them. Spitters (featured, x3 weight) leave puddles that stack with the static acid pools, so safe ground shrinks; spore pods hide packs in clouds you have to burn or blast. Creep grows from nests and makes you slow and them fast, and fire (dash, barrels, Incendiary) is the only way to win ground back.

floors.events: Teach rain: the first pulse comes at 15 s with a long 5 s warning and a 'GET UNDER COVER' hint pointing to the nearest roof. Enemies caught in the rain visibly sizzle and the first kill by rain pops a 'THE RAIN HURTS THEM TOO' toast. Spitters arrive in wave 2 in pairs from across the central acid ring.

Twist: the purifier G sits under the only big roof, and it is immune to rain but not to Spitters. Four Spore Pods are pre-placed on the approaches; their clouds hide the packs walking to the purifier. Rain at 10 s, 30 s. At 25 s the purifier vents (a 4 m green burst) that clears every puddle and spore cloud around it: a breather if you stayed close.

Rot Fields: three nests feed creep across the fields. Rows of red barrels sit on the creep; every barrel chain scorches a band. Kill the nests first or the creep keeps outgrowing you. Acid rain does not scorch creep, but enemies on creep regenerate through it, so rain is weaker here: the zone's lesson flips. An Incendiary Rounds drop is guaranteed at 20 s.

Monsoon: rain every 12 s, and each roof corrodes: after 2 pulses a roof slab drips, hisses and falls (it becomes rubble, a C for 15 s, then open floor). By the end only two roofs stand, so the hero is forced to migrate across the map between pulses. A Mender at 30 s heals a Carapace-less pack, and the rain cannot kill what it heals: find it.
Mire Pit: an arena of acid pools with six roofs. Rain pulses every 20 s all fight and hurt the boss too, but only while she is outside cover.

boss.name: Mire Matriarch (the Acid Matriarch from enemies-and-powerups.md, promoted to a zone boss)
boss.body: HP 220. Phase 1 (100-65%): the doc's Volley (5 globs in a fan) and Acid Field (30% of the floor turns to acid for 6 s, always with a safe path). Twist: she walks under a roof before every rain pulse and is immune there, so the hero has to drag her out with Volley range (she keeps 10-14 m away and backs off when you push). A Matriarch caught in the rain takes 3 RH per tick and shrieks. Phase 2 (65-30%): Pool Dive. She sinks into an acid pool (1.0 s) and surfaces from another one 2 s later, with a green ring telegraph on the target pool; two Spitters climb out of the pool she left. Spore Pods sprout on her surface spots. Shoot pods before she arrives or the next volley comes out of a cloud. Phase 3 (30-0%): Bring the Storm. She calls the rain herself every 10 s and starts melting roofs she stands under (3 s). Corroded roofs fall like Monsoon. Counterplay: keep a roof between you and her line, and bait her into ones that are already melting. Death: a 6 m acid burst that also scorches all creep in the arena.
boss.look: Spitter placeholder (Drone model) at 3.0x, tinted bile green #6f9a2a with a toxic #9bff3a emissive abdomen sphere 1.8x larger than the Spitter's, a crown of six Lancer spikes, and a dripping green particle trail. Name banner: MIRE MATRIARCH, 'Mother of the rain.'

modifiers: Acid Downpour: rain every 12 s instead of 20 s.
Overgrowth: creep starts on 25% of floor cells on every floor and grows 30% faster.
Toxic Swarm: 20% of enemies gain the Toxic modifier (acid trails).
Leaky Roofs: every roof stops protecting 1 s before the rain ends.

rewards.first_clear: Incendiary Rounds drop weight x2 in this zone and a "Burn the creep" hint card unlocks, plus +10 Cores.
rewards.replay: Biomass and Commander XP farm: rain kills count as hero kills and drop full biomass, so a roof-camping build levels up faster here than anywhere else in Act II.

stars.3: Clear the boss without taking acid rain damage.
stars.bonus: Let the acid rain kill 40 enemies in one run.

layout_notes.marsh-a: Boardwalk. A broken acid ring around a central island, boardwalk gaps on the diagonals, roofs and shallow ponds in the corners.
layout_notes.marsh-b: Pump Island. Purifier under a 3x2 roof in the centre, acid channels running diagonally, four spore pods on the approaches, small roofs spread to the edges.
layout_notes.marsh-c: Rot Fields. Long creep fields between rows of feed bins, three nests in a triangle, barrel rows across the creep.
layout_notes.marsh-boss: Mire Pit. Six acid pools for the Matriarch to dive between, six roofs, open mud between.

name: Helix Data Vault
pitch: A cold, humming server fortress the hive is trying to read: steal its cores through laser lattices and dark aisles while cloaked Stalkers hunt you between the racks.

theme.floor: Raised black floor tiles #15181c with a cyan grid line #2fd0ff every 2 m; electrified grates steel #5b6168; dark aisles d have no grid glow
theme.walls: Server racks as B blocks, matte black #101317 with blinking LED strips (emissive cyan #39d7ff and amber #ffb000 noise texture); vault walls brushed steel #8a9099
theme.lighting: Key light cold white-cyan #cfefff, intensity 0.7, straight down 80 deg (ceiling panels); ambient #1a2a36 at 0.3; rack LEDs carry most of the mood; dark aisles fall to black
theme.signature_detail: Laser fences cross the aisles in red #ff3355; the floor grid ripples cyan outward from every grate pulse; captured data cores float above the hero's shoulder like a hologram
theme.audio: Server fan drone and relay clicks, laser hum, the 'clean' synthetic voice of the vault ('Unauthorised biological presence'), Stalker hiss cutting through it

signature: The vault is a timing puzzle under fire. Laser fences turn aisles into gates that open 3 s in every 8, so you plan routes on the beat; grates are death floors for the swarm when they pulse and the breaker is a one-way choice (switch them off to be safe, or keep them to keep killing). Dark aisles hide Stalkers (featured) and only the hero's light and light pylons expose them; turrets watch the long aisles and pull the swarm off you. Fewer enemies than other Act II zones, but every one of them is a question.

floors.events: Server Hall. Teach grates: the four aisle grates pulse in sync and wave 1 runs straight across them, so the first pulse kills half a pack and a 'LURE THEM ACROSS' hint fires. The breaker K in the north-east corner is shown with a 'shoot to switch off grates for good' tooltip; most players should learn to leave it.

Cold Storage. Six data cores in the cold aisles, three of them in dark (d) bays. Each pickup triggers its ambush from the nearest S and the vault voice reads out a 'LOCKDOWN' that switches the laser fences to 4 s on / 4 s off for 10 s. First Stalkers: they wait in the dark bays and de-cloak on the hero as he grabs a core. Two light pylons let you pre-light a bay before you go in.

Firewall Ring. The relays sit in a ring around the core room, each behind a laser fence. Relay 1 opens the inner fence of the west wing and turns on the first turret; relay 2 switches every grate on (the swarm now has to cross them to reach you); relay 3 drops the core room's fences and ends the floor. Each relay is 3 s, but taking a hit knocks 15% off, so clear the room or capture the turret first.

floors.params: kill 'Ghostkey' within 60 s for the bonus
floors.events: The marked elite is Ghostkey, a Shade Stalker carrying a stolen core. It flees through the dark bays and laser lattice and summons escorts every 10 s; when revealed it drops a decoy shimmer. The lights go out floor-wide at 20 s (dark=true) until the hero lights both pylons; Ghostkey's eye glints are gold so they are trackable. Lancers on the far racks punish chasing in straight lines.
Core Chamber. Four turrets, a grate cross through the middle, laser fences that seal the quadrants in Phase 2, two light pylons and a breaker for Phase 3's blackout.

boss.name: WARDEN-9
boss.body: The vault's security frame, now wired with hive tissue. HP 230, slow walk 0.5x, armour front 50%. Phase 1 (100-65%): Suppression. A minigun sweep: a red cone (60 deg, 14 m) telegraphs for 1.0 s and then sweeps for 2 s (10 HP per 0.25 s); server racks and crates block it. Every 15 s it hacks one neutral turret red: a red turret fires at the hero until recaptured (2.5 s), and a recaptured turret prioritises WARDEN-9 and does 3x damage to it. Phase 2 (65-30%): Lockdown. Laser fences seal the arena into four quadrants for 5 s of every 8; WARDEN walks through fences unharmed but takes 6 RH/s on a live grate like any enemy. It chases the hero, so luring it across the central grate cross on the pulse is the damage window. The breaker K shuts the grates off: you get safety, it gets a free floor. Phase 3 (30-0%): Blackout. The lights die (floor-wide DARKNESS) and WARDEN cloaks Stalker-style between sweeps; only its red visor glint shows. Light the two pylons to expose it (+20% damage) and watch for the red cone, which still shows in the dark. Two Stalkers join. Death: it powers down, kneels, the core floats out (bonus Weapon Parts).
boss.look: Iron Vanguard hero model at 2.0x, tinted gunmetal #2d3238 with a red emissive visor #ff3355 and purple creep veins #b04dff on the limbs (emissive vertex noise); the Vanguard minigun at 2.0x; three thin red line renderers from its back to the nearest turret while hacking. Name banner: WARDEN-9, 'Access denied.'

modifiers: Lockdown Protocol: every laser fence runs 6 s on, 2 s off.
Black Site: every floor is dark; flares refill at 2 caches per floor.
Ghost Protocol: 20% of non-Stalker enemies gain Cloaked.
Overclocked: grates pulse twice as often and their current travels 1 cell further.

rewards.first_clear: Decoy Hologram joins the drop pool (it baits Stalkers and turrets), and the "Helix" vault banner, plus +10 Cores.
rewards.replay: Each data core collected on the SALVAGE floor pays a small Credits bonus, and the ASSASSINATE floor is the cleanest Stalker practice in the game before Act III.

stars.3: Kill Ghostkey within 60 s on the ASSASSINATE floor.
stars.bonus: Kill 40 enemies with electrified grates in one run, without shooting the breaker.

layout_notes.vault-a: Server Hall. Four long rack rows with grates in the aisles, a breaker in the north-east corner, turrets at each end of the centre aisle.
layout_notes.vault-b: Cold Storage. A diagonal staircase of rack blocks with dark bays between them; laser fences gate the bays; six cores, a lift in the south-east, two pylons and a flare cache.
layout_notes.vault-c: Firewall Ring. A square ring corridor around the core room, relays at three corners behind fences, grates on the inner ring, turrets on the outer ring.
layout_notes.vault-boss: Core Chamber. Open chamber, grate cross in the middle, laser fences on the quadrant lines, turrets in the four quadrants, pylons and breaker on the edges.

name: Deepcut Mine
pitch: A collapsing deep-core mine where the swarm swims through rock: read the dust, ride the ore cart through the dark, blow the shaft behind you and face the thing that ate the mine.

theme.floor: Packed ore-dust #4a3a2c with rail sleepers #3a2a1e; steel blast plates #6f7a82 (the blue zone '~' reskinned as metal plates, Burrowers cannot surface on them); crumbling walkways cracked rock #5c4836
theme.walls: Rough rock blocks #3b2f26 with ochre seams #b07a3a; timber pit props as thin brown posts on every B corner; crates as ore skips
theme.lighting: Key light dim amber #ffcf8a, intensity 0.45, 70 deg overhead (string lamps); ambient #2a2018 at 0.25; floors 2-5 go dark (DARKNESS) with the hero's head lamp and amber pylons; pits glow faint red #ff3a2a from below
theme.signature_detail: Dust trickles from the ceiling 2 s before every cave-in circle, so rocks are readable even in the dark; Burrower dust trails glow faintly in the head-lamp beam
theme.audio: Deep rumbles and timber groans, dripping water, the cart's iron wheels, the Burrower's rising grind, a distant thud that is The Maw moving under the floor

signature: The ground is the enemy. Burrowers (featured) come from below, cave-ins come from above (35 HP rocks that leave rubble for 15 s), and the pits in between are where Shove, shotgun and explosions turn into instant kills. Steel plates are islands where Burrowers cannot surface. From floor 2 the lights are out, so the head lamp, flares and light pylons decide what auto-fire can shoot. Crumbling walkways make every route a one-way decision: you can cross it once, and whatever follows you falls.

floors.events: Lamp Gallery, still lit. Teach pits: wave 1 Drones path round the chasms, and a free Shove card is offered at the start so pit kills happen on the first floor. Teach cave-ins: from wave 2, 2 rock circles every 9 s, and rubble from each lasts 15 s. The crumbling walkway in the middle is shown with a 'it falls behind you' toast the first time it drops a pack.

floors.params: ore cart through the dark, 400 HP
floors.events: Ore Line, lights out. The cart carries the floor's only big light (a 6 m amber lamp on its prow), so pushing it forward also moves your safe vision. Three light pylons along the track light whole bends for good once you stand on them; flare caches at both turns. Burrowers surface under the cart (it takes the eruption) unless the hero stands on a steel plate nearby. A cave-in blocks the track at the halfway point: rubble must be shot (15 RH) before the cart can roll.

The Tremor: the gallery is dark this time, and the mine shakes every 15 s (screen shake 0.2, 4 rock circles at once). At 30 s the crumbling walkway collapses by itself and two new pits open where the circles land (they become '_' for the rest of the floor), so the arena loses floor as you fight. Carapaces charge across the gallery: bait them into a pit's edge and shove them in.

floors.params: 3 charges, then 25 s to the lift
floors.events: Collapse Shaft. Three charges lie beyond a chasm crossed only by three crumbling bridges. Each bridge carries you once, so the route is: cross one, plant the three charges, and use another bridge to get back to the lift before the blast. Cave-ins every 6 s during the countdown and a Splitter pack comes out of the charge tunnel the moment the last charge is set. If a bridge is gone, a Leaper pounce shows you the jump the swarm can make and you cannot.
The Throat. A dark arena around a central pit with four steel plate islands and two pylons. Rocks fall every time The Maw dives.

boss.name: The Maw (from enemies-and-powerups.md, Act II finale)
boss.body: HP 300, only damageable while surfaced. Keeps the doc's three phases and ties each to the mine. Phase 1 (100-60%): Breach and Tremor Lines as in the doc. Every dive brings down 3 rock circles; rubble from them blocks Tremor Lines, so standing behind fresh rubble is safe. Phase 2 (60-25%): Twin Breach plus 3 Burrowers; each breach now cracks the floor around its ring, and the cracked cells become crumbling walkways (k) that fall when stepped on. The arena slowly turns into islands. Pylons light the arena for good; in the dark only the dust rings are visible. Phase 3 (25-0%): Devour, surfacing in the central pit. The pull drags everything toward the pit for 4 s; Drones it eats heal it 2 HP each, but Drones you shove or blow into the pit first are lost to it (no heal). Standing on a steel plate stops the pull, exactly as the doc says, and the plates are the only place the 360 spit cannot reach behind rubble. Win condition feel: the last 25% is a race to clear adds before it can eat them.
boss.look: Column of 4 stacked Bloater meshes (scaled 1.6, 1.4, 1.2, 1.0) tinted dusty brown #6b5238 with a red emissive mouth ring #ff3a2a (as in the doc); Burrower dust at 3x; a ring of 8 Lancer spikes as teeth inside the mouth. Name banner: THE MAW, 'The mine was never empty.'

modifiers: Unstable: cave-ins every 5 s on every floor, and rubble lasts 30 s.
Deep Dark: every floor is dark from floor 1, and flare caches are halved.
Burrowing Swarm: 15% of Drones travel underground like Burrowers and surface in pairs.
Rich Seam: every pit kill drops +1 biomass and a Weapon Part (a farming modifier).

rewards.first_clear: Act II finale: opens Act III and Swarm Gate, the Stasis Field power-up joins the drop pool, plus +20 Cores.
rewards.replay: The Maw is the Act II boss to farm on Hard and Nightmare for first-clear Cores; the Rich Seam modifier (pit kills drop Weapon Parts) makes it a Hot Zone favourite.

stars.3: Kill 40 enemies by pits or collapsing walkways in one run.
stars.bonus: Finish the DETONATE floor with 10 s or more left on the countdown.

layout_notes.mine-a: Lamp Gallery. Irregular chasms on the left, top and right, a crumbling walkway down the middle, two steel-plate islands, two pylons and a flare cache.
layout_notes.mine-b: Ore Line. A long S-shaped rail from the north-west down to the south: tunnels between rock pillars, pits beside the track, pylons and flare caches at the turns.
layout_notes.mine-c: Collapse Shaft. Lift and spawn on the north side, a two-cell chasm across the middle with three crumbling bridges, three charges in the south galleries.
layout_notes.mine-boss: The Throat. Central pit, four steel-plate islands, a ring of crumbling floor in the south, rock pillars and two pylons.

name: St. Aster Quarantine
pitch: A sealed hospital where the infection has started rebuilding the building: hive walls grow across corridors, toxic vents breathe on a rhythm, and the healers on the other side keep the swarm alive.

theme.floor: Clinical white-green tiles #cfe0d6 stained with creep #2a0f33; red cross floor markings #c0392b at med stations; toxic vents behind green grates
theme.walls: Hospital partitions as B blocks, off-white #e6ece8 with mint trim #7fd8a6 and torn plastic quarantine sheeting (thin translucent quads, alpha 0.3); beds and trolleys are the cargo crate model scaled 1.0x0.5x0.6 in white
theme.lighting: Key light flickering fluorescent #e9fff2, intensity 0.85, 85 deg straight down, with a random 0.1 s flicker every 4-9 s; ambient #4a6a5a at 0.4; red emergency lamps #ff2a2a (3 m) above every blast door; creep veins add purple #b04dff glow
theme.fog: Disinfectant haze turning sick: #b9d6c4 at the start of a floor, lerping to #6a4a7a as creep spreads, linear 22-55 m
theme.signature_detail: The PA keeps playing a calm evacuation announcement that slowly distorts as creep coverage rises; hive walls grow up through the floor tiles with a wet cracking sound
theme.audio: Fluorescent buzz, a heart monitor flatline loop in the distance, vents hissing on their 6 s rhythm, Mender chimes (a soft rising tone) whenever a heal lands

signature: The building fights back. Toxic vents erupt on a readable 6 s beat (18 HP per tick to you, 4 RH/s to them), so the best tactic is dragging the pack through a vent column on its warning beat. Hive walls block corridors but can be shot down (explosions x3) to open a shortcut or a firing line, and they grow back in 12 s, so routes are temporary. Egg clusters sit in every ward and creep spreads from walls and nests. Menders and Weavers (featured) are the zone's question: the swarm here does not die until you find who is healing it and who is closing the doors.

floors.events: Triage Hall. Teach vents: four toxic vent columns flank the hall and wave 1 is a pure Drone flood that runs straight through them. Teach Menders: wave 2 brings two Carapaces with a Mender each; a green-tether hint fires on the first heal. Hive walls ring the centre and the first one you shoot regrows in front of you, with a '12 s' timer ring.

Isolation Wing. Four sealed wards. Weavers web every doorway you need to hack. Twist: a hive wall between the first ward and the lift ward is a shortcut. Shoot it down (10 RH) and you can skip the two middle wards, but both of their spawns come with you into the lift ward on top of its own, and the wall regrows behind you. Taking the long route is safer and gives two +35 HP room clears.

Cure Lab. The synthesiser G sits inside a ring of hive walls with four gaps. Weavers string webs across the gaps so the hero's way in is closed while enemies walk through. The Surgeon (mini-boss) arrives at 20 s: it re-grows hive walls instantly and tethers to the synthesiser's attackers. Vents ring the lab: luring the attack waves across them on the beat is how you keep the generator alive.

floors.params: 3 charges, then 25 s to the lift
floors.events: Sterilise the ward. Three charges sit inside the hive-walled centre and in the east and west wings. On the last plant the vents go to a 3 s cycle (sterilisation gas) and all egg clusters hatch at once (HATCH_ALL). The 25 s run to the lift goes through the vent columns, so the timing of the gas decides your route. Hive walls between you and the lift regrow on a 6 s timer during the countdown.
Ward Zero. A round ward with creep at the centre, eight toxic vents, four hive wall arcs and egg clusters at the edges.

miniboss.name: The Surgeon
miniboss.body: Floor 3 mini-boss, HP 60, speed 0.8x. A grown Mender that operates on the hive. Tether: it links to up to 3 allies at once (2 HP/s each) and, unlike a normal Mender, to the hive walls around the synthesiser, which it regrows instantly when shot down. Every 12 s: Transfusion. It pulls 20% HP from every Drone in 8 m (they visibly shrink and die) and heals itself with it, so leaving fodder alive near it is a mistake. At 50%: it seals itself behind a hive wall cocoon (30 RH, explosions x3) and 2 Menders arrive. Counterplay: kill the Drones near it first, burn or freeze its wards (fire and ice block healing), and drag it through a vent on the eruption: vents deal double damage to it and cancel the current tether.
miniboss.look: Mender placeholder (Drone 1.1x) scaled to 2.6x, tinted surgical white #e6efe9 with a mint green emissive sac #7fd8a6 and four thin Lancer spikes as scalpels; three green tether lines at once. Name banner: THE SURGEON, 'Do no harm.'

boss.name: Patient Zero
boss.body: The first infected, half man and half hive. HP 260, speed 0.7x. Phase 1 (100-65%): Contagion. It walks toward the hero and every 8 s Coughs a toxic cone (8 m, 50 deg, 1.0 s green preview) that leaves creep where it lands. Creep under Patient Zero heals it 2% max HP/s (the zone's SPREAD rule), so scorching the floor it fights on is the first priority: dash through creep, blow barrels, use Incendiary. Phase 2 (65-30%): Quarantine Lines. It slams the floor and hive walls burst up in two straight lines that cut the arena in four for 12 s; each quarter holds egg clusters that hatch in 6 s. Shoot through a wall (explosions x3) to keep the fight in one room, or use the time to clear eggs. Vents in its quarter erupt on its own cycle: a vent hit on Patient Zero stuns it for 1.5 s. Phase 3 (30-0%): Outbreak. It splits: two Menders peel off its back and tether to it; until both die it takes 50% damage. The creep at the centre grows 3x faster and the vents run 4 s cycles. Death: it collapses into a hive wall statue that stays in the arena.
boss.look: Iron Vanguard hero model at 1.8x, tinted pale sick grey-green #9aa898 with creep veins #b04dff pulsing over the body, a Bloater mesh at 0.8x fused on its back (emissive purple pus), torn hospital sheeting (translucent quad) hanging off one arm. Name banner: PATIENT ZERO, 'It started with him.'

modifiers: Pandemic: creep spreads at double rate and its cap rises to 60% of walkable cells.
Overcrowded Ward: every egg cluster hatches 5 Drones instead of 3.
Field Medics: every pack of 8+ comes with a Mender.
Sealed Wing: hive walls regrow in 6 s instead of 12 s.

rewards.first_clear: Med Gel drop weight x1.5 across Act III and a "Find the healer" hint card, plus +15 Cores.
rewards.replay: The ESCAPE floor's hive-wall shortcut is a speedrun route for the par-time star, and Patient Zero is a strong Hot Zone pick for Alloy.

stars.3: Kill every Mender before it heals anything on the DEFEND floor (any Mender heal fails the star).
stars.bonus: Kill 25 enemies with toxic vents in one run.

layout_notes.ward-a: Triage Hall. Bed rows north and south, two hive-wall arcs around the centre, four vent columns, charges in the wings and the centre, lift in the south-east.
layout_notes.ward-b: Isolation Wing. Four wards in a square loop with blast doors and hacks; a hive wall in the west wall is the shortcut from the first ward to the lift ward.
layout_notes.ward-c: Cure Lab. Synthesiser in a hive-wall ring with four gaps, vents on the diagonals, creep patches and eggs in the corners.
layout_notes.ward-boss: Ward Zero. Round ward, creep at the centre, eight vents, four hive wall arcs, egg clusters on the edges, one med station.

name: Tyndall Relay Spire
pitch: A comms tower above the clouds in a permanent lightning storm: hide under steel from the sky, snipe the snipers, and hold the uplink on dishes where the wind wants to throw you off the edge.

theme.floor: Steel deck plates #5e6670 with yellow edge stripes at every drop; cable runs and electrified grates #4c5258; landing dishes '~' painted white #e8eef2 with a red ring
theme.walls: Antenna housings and equipment racks as B blocks, white #dfe5ea with red aviation stripes #c8321e; storm shutters as crates in grey #7a8288
theme.lighting: Key light storm blue-violet #9fb0ff, intensity 0.6, 40 deg from the left; ambient #2a3048 at 0.35; lightning flashes spike a white directional #ffffff to 2.5 for 0.1 s; red aviation beacons #ff2a2a (4 m) blinking 0.5 Hz on every B corner
theme.fog: Cloud sea #5a6488, linear 18-50 m, with cloud layers scrolling below the pit cells
theme.signature_detail: Before every lightning circle a thin blue spark crawls up the nearest antenna, so the strike pattern reads from the tower; spent strikes leave scorch marks that glow for 3 s
theme.audio: Howling wind bed, thunder 0.3-1.0 s after each flash, static bursts on the comms loop, the Lancer's laser hum and lock click carrying over the storm

signature: The sky is a second enemy and cover is the answer to both of them. Lightning STRIKES (35 HP, 12 RH to enemies) fall every 6 s, half on you, and roofs (u) block them, the same roofs that block the Lancers' (featured) lines. Wind gusts every 12 s push everything one way for 3 s: toward the edge pits that is lethal for the swarm and dangerous for you, so you fight upwind and let the gusts clear the deck. Grates carry the storm's current; the breaker turns them off, at the cost of your best killing floor. Stand still and the Lancers and lightning find you; move and the wind decides where you end up.

floors.events: Lower Ring. Teach lightning and cover together: the first strike is aimed at the roof you stand under and bounces off it with a 'COVER BLOCKS LIGHTNING' toast. Lancers arrive in wave 2 on the far side of the central housing, so the first trace teaches breaking line of sight. Wind is off on this floor; the pit corners are just for shoves.

Cable Run. A switchback climb through the cable trays; each relay restores one antenna section. Relay 1 turns off the first grate field; relay 2 brings the wind online (gusts from the west); relay 3 turns the lightning into a storm (strikes every 4 s); relay 4 ends the floor. The breaker sits in the middle: shooting it kills every grate (safer climb) but also the floor's best Drone killer.

floors.params: kill 'Highwire' within 60 s for the bonus
floors.events: The same cable run, now in a gale (west gusts every 10 s). The target is the mini-boss Highwire, a Marksman Lancer that flees up and down the switchbacks, stopping only to fire from roofs. Lightning cannot hit it while it is under a roof, but it can hit you; the chase is about cutting it off at the bends. Escort summons every 10 s are Lancer pairs that cover its retreat.

Summit Dishes. Three landing dishes on the summit, split by the central shaft and two jump-pad pairs. The uplink ring hops between dishes every 10 s, and the dishes have no roofs: lightning every 5 s targets the ring. Wind gusts alternate east and west, pushing toward the edge pits on both sides. A Shrieker hides behind the north housings; a Mender keeps two Carapaces alive in the ring.
Crown Platform. Four antenna pylons, a ring of grates, four roofs and pit corners. Wind on, lightning every 6 s, and both are her weapons until you turn them against her.

miniboss.name: Highwire
miniboss.body: Floor 3 ASSASSINATE target and mini-boss, HP 55 (the 4x HP elite rule), speed 0.9x. A Marksman Lancer (3-spine fan) that never stops moving. Rail Run: it sprints along the cable trays at 1.4x and is untargetable while on a grate that is live (the current shields it), so the breaker is the fastest way to make it killable, at the cost of the grates. Perch: it stops only under roofs to fire a 3-spine fan (1.4 s trace, 0.35 s lock); lightning cannot reach it there. Gust Jump: when a gust blows, it rides it 6 m downwind, which is how it escapes; stand downwind of it and the gust brings it to you. At 50%: it drops a Decoy shimmer (Stalker rule) and calls 2 Lancers. Counterplay: break its lines with housings, cut the corners on the switchbacks, and use the wind.
miniboss.look: Lancer placeholder (Spitter-shaped Drone 1.2x with the back spike) at 1.8x, tinted dark teal #1f4f55 with a gold elite rim, three back spikes instead of one, a cyan spark trail while it runs on grates. Name banner: HIGHWIRE, 'Eyes on the storm.'

boss.name: The Arc Matron
boss.body: A queen Weaver that has wrapped the spire's crown in her web and feeds on the storm. HP 280. Phase 1 (100-65%): Charged Web. She strings electrified strands between the four antenna pylons (Matron Weaver rule: 8 damage on touch), 3 at a time; each strand lasts 12 s. Lightning that hits a strand arcs along it (15 HP to anything touching it, enemies included). Shoot strands (3 HP) or let the wind snap them (gusts break strands parallel to the gust). Phase 2 (65-30%): Lightning Rod. She climbs a pylon (2 s) and becomes the storm's target: lightning every 4 s, but each strike near her heals her 10 HP unless the pylon's base grate is off. Every pylon has a grate under it; shooting the breaker drops all four, and a Matron on a dead pylon takes the strike instead (12 RH and a 2 s fall stun). She also calls Lancers from the edges. Phase 3 (30-0%): Storm Cradle. She comes down and spins a web dome over the roofs, cutting the hero off from cover; gusts every 8 s push toward the pit corners and lightning falls every 3 s. Burn or shoot your way into a roof, fight from under it, and let her chase you through the open where the storm hits her too. Death: the storm breaks, sunlight floods the platform for the reward screen.
boss.look: Leaper model at 2.8x (the Weaver recipe), tinted ivory #ece4d0 with dark purple joints and a cyan #5fd8ff emissive abdomen that crackles (spark particles) whenever lightning lands within 6 m; strands are the Weaver tracer cylinder in cyan. Name banner: THE ARC MATRON, 'She weaves the storm.'

modifiers: Superstorm: lightning every 3 s, and one in four strikes chains to the nearest unit within 4 m.
Hurricane: gusts every 8 s from a random direction (2 s warning still applies).
Sniper Nest: Lancer max alive +2, and every Lancer is a Marksman (3-spine fan).
Torn Roofs: half the roofs are missing on every floor.

rewards.first_clear: Tesla Coil joins the drop pool at double weight (storm flavour) and the "Tyndall" storm banner, plus +15 Cores.
rewards.replay: Lightning kills count toward a weekly Daily Op family ("storm kills"), and the Superstorm modifier makes this the Hot Zone for fast Credits clears.

stars.3: Let lightning kill 30 enemies in one run.
stars.bonus: Kill Highwire within 60 s without shooting the breaker.

layout_notes.spire-a: Lower Ring. A deck around the central antenna housing, four roofs on the sides, two pairs of housings, pit corners at the edge.
layout_notes.spire-b: Cable Run. A switchback climb from the north-west, through cable trays and grate fields, to the south; relays at each turn, breaker in the middle.
layout_notes.spire-c: Summit Dishes. Two dishes split by a central shaft and joined by two jump-pad pairs, a third dish on the south deck, roofs between them, edge pits east and west.
layout_notes.spire-boss: Crown Platform. Four antenna pylons in a square with grates between them, four roofs, pit corners, breaker on the east edge.
